## Passive tracers per dry air, with an optional upper bound (`scalar`) {#sec-ch10-tracer}

@sec-ch01 maps the scalar transport path and derives how the ratio rides with the implicit dry transfer and with
dry-density sources (@sec-ch01-scalar, @sec-ch01-stage, @eq-ch01-stage-upwind, @eq-ch01-stage-dry). This section
adds what makes those tracers part of the moist coupling: why the reference mass is dry air and not total mass,
the second limiter that bounds the ratio from above, and the conditions under which that bound holds.

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Keeps tracers as ratios $r_n$[^rg-6b0954b378f1] per dry mass, non-negative and optionally at most $b$; @eq-ch10-tracer-bound.

**Data.** Reads $\rho_{\mathrm d}r_n$ and the hydro dry-mass fluxes; writes the tracers' stage tendency on interior cells.

**Placement.** Every RK stage after the hydro fluxes; positivity limiter first, complement bound second.

**Activation.** YAML `scalar` (`nvar` or `names`[^rg-28a461114d30]); `upper-bound`[^rg-a7c011b0d04d] default $-1$ (off), 0 refused, positive needs the limiter.

**Guarantee / limits.** $r_n\ge0$; $r_n\le b$ while the mass Courant number is below one and $\rho_{\mathrm d}$ moves by transport only.

**Evidence.** @tbl-ch10-tracer-tests; `test_scalar.release`, `test_tracer_dry_convention_python`, `tracer_check.py` `[C1]`–`[C5]`.
:::

Local symbols: $b$ is the upper bound of a tracer's mixing ratio (YAML `scalar/upper-bound`); $F_n$ and
$F_{\mathrm d}$ are the $x_1$ face fluxes of tracer $n$ and of dry air, and $F^{\mathrm c}_n=bF_{\mathrm d}-F_n$ the flux of
the complement $b\rho_{\mathrm d}-\rho_{\mathrm d}r_n$; $J^{\mathrm d}_{i-1/2}$ [kg] is the implicit dry-air transfer through
a face, positive upward, as in @sec-ch01-stage.

A mixing ratio is a mass per unit dry mass, $r_n=\rho_n/\rho_{\mathrm d}$, and is what a tracer here carries. The
vapour and condensate rows of the state carry instead the mass fraction per unit total mass, $y_n$ with
$\rho_n=\rho y_n$ (appendix A, notation group 2), so a species given as a mixing ratio enters the state as
$y_n = r_n\rho_{\mathrm d}/\rho$.

A tracer measured per unit total mass would change its ratio whenever water condenses, evaporates or settles out of
a cell, although no tracer moved. Per unit dry mass the ratio changes only when dry air moves, which every moist
operator of this chapter leaves alone: the saturation adjustment, the borrow, the column repair and the kinetics write
species rows only, and sedimentation moves condensate, not dry air.

### Derivation

Write $\rho_{\mathrm d}r_n$ for the tracer density, so the code's `r = u / rho` with `rho` the dry density is $r_n$
({{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::forward >}}). The $x_1$ transport flux is
$F_n=F_{\mathrm d}\,r_n^{\mathrm{up}}$ with the upwind ratio, so a uniform ratio stays uniform under it; under the
implicit dry transfer the tracer increment is $r_n$ times the dry increment (`[C3]`),[^trc-c] so it stays uniform
there too. The donor cap on that transfer (@sec-ch01-stage) limits each tracer transfer to what its donor holds plus
its inflow from below; for a uniform ratio it does not bind, and where a ratio is not uniform it keeps every tracer
density non-negative. On $x_2$ and $x_3$ faces the face-flux covariance, on by default, changes the flux: the scalar is
upwinded with the dry-mass flux less its covariance row and adds its own tracer row, the row of a hydro species with
the same mass fraction, `scalar_flux_covariance`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::scalar_flux_covariance >}}; @sec-ch04-fluxcov).

Why the complement limiter bounds $r_n$ from above:

1. *The complement.* If $r_n\le b$ then $b\rho_{\mathrm d}-\rho_{\mathrm d}r_n\ge0$.
2. *Its flux.* When $\rho_{\mathrm d}$ moves only by its own divergence, the complement is transported by
   $F^{\mathrm c}_n=bF_{\mathrm d}-F_n$ (`[C4]`, sympy).
3. *The same limiter.* Non-negativity of a transported density is what the positivity limiter enforces, so the code
   applies it to $F^{\mathrm c}_n$, which returns a factor $\Theta\in[0,1]$ per face.
4. *Put back only the change:*

$$
F_n \leftarrow F_n + (1-\Theta)\,\big(bF_{\mathrm d}-F_n\big) = \Theta F_n + (1-\Theta)\,bF_{\mathrm d}.
$$ {#eq-ch10-tracer-bound}

5. *A blend.* The second form of @eq-ch10-tracer-bound is a blend between the tracer's own flux and the flux of a
   tracer sitting at the bound, so a plateau at $b$ keeps advecting (`[C1]`, symbolic). It is applied as `h - g` in
   `ScalarImpl::forward` when `upper_bound` is positive ({{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::forward >}}).
   This section is the home of that bound's derivation; @sec-ch08-scalar covers the call of the positivity limiter
   it reuses.
6. *Round-off.* Adding the change leaves $F_n$ bitwise unchanged on every face where $\Theta=1$, because
   $h-g$ is then an exact zero. Recomputing $bF_{\mathrm d}-F^{\mathrm c}_n$ instead rounds twice and perturbs many faces
   by up to an ulp of $bF_{\mathrm d}$: 9994 of 10000 in a float32 test (`[C2]`) and 3039 of 10000 on uniform random
   fluxes (`[C5]`). The count depends on the input; the bitwise result where $\Theta=1$ does not.
7. *The premise.* The bound inherits the positivity limiter's premise: it holds while the mass Courant number stays
   below one and $\rho_{\mathrm d}$ changes only by the transport divergence. The implicit vertical correction and any
   forcing that writes the dry row break that premise, as the code comment states.

[^trc-c]: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch10/checks/tracer_check.py`, output `tracer_check.out`, lines `[C1]`–`[C5]`; a numpy
    and sympy port of the complement bound in `ScalarImpl::forward` and of the implicit tracer transfer in
    `MeshBlockImpl::advance_local` at the pin, double and float32.
    Run on CPU, one process, with Python 3.12.10, sympy 1.14.0 and numpy 2.5.3; the output matches the committed file.

### Numerical method

The ratio is reconstructed with the scalar block's `reconstruct`, or the hydro's horizontal one when the card omits it, and upwinded with the hydro dry-mass flux
`flux1[IDN]` (and `flux2`, `flux3`, with the covariance rows above); the Riemann solver must be `upwind`. With the
EOS limiter on, or whenever the scalar carries its covariance row, the positivity limiter scales the tracer fluxes
first; the complement limiter, if `upper-bound` > 0, scales them second. The `divergence` then gives the stage
tendency on interior cells only ({{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::forward >}}).
The implicit dry transfer and the dry-source carry follow, as in @sec-ch01-stage. @fig-ch10-tracer-face shows the
donor choice of that transfer.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch10-tracer-face
#| fig-cap: "Donor choice of the implicit dry transfer $J^{\\mathrm d}_{i-1/2}$ at one $x_1$ face, between cells $i-1$ and $i$. Sky-blue dots are the cell ratios, the orange triangle the face, the orange arrow the direction of the dry transfer. (a) An upward transfer carries the ratio of the cell below; (b) a downward transfer carries the ratio of the cell above."
#| fig-alt: "Two panels, each with two stacked cells and a face between them; an arrow points up in (a) and down in (b), with the transported ratio written beside it."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch10.figures.fig_tracer_face import make_fig
make_fig()
```

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| YAML keys | {{< code src/scalar/scalar_options.cpp ScalarOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}} | `from_yaml` | `scalar` |
| setup checks | {{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::reset >}} | `ScalarImpl::reset` | `upper-bound` |
| positivity limiter | {{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::forward >}} | `flux_positivity_theta` | `limiter`, or the scalar's covariance row |
| complement bound | {{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::forward >}} | `upper_bound` | `upper-bound` |
| implicit transfer | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}} | `mass_corr` | |

: Code map of the dry-air tracers; @sec-ch01 holds the rest of the scalar
path (@tbl-ch01-scalar-code). {#tbl-ch10-tracer-code}

1. Parse the keys; `upper_bound` defaults to $-1$ ({{< code src/scalar/scalar_options.cpp ScalarOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}).
2. Refuse a solver other than `upwind`, a bound of 0, and a bound without the limiter, `TORCH_CHECK`
   ({{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::reset >}}).
3. Form the ratio per dry air, `rho` ({{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::forward >}}).
4. Limit for positivity, `theta` ({{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::forward >}}).
5. Limit the complement and add the change, `flux_positivity_scale_`
   ({{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::forward >}}).
6. Take the `divergence` on interior cells ({{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::forward >}}).

The setup refusals are listed with the card above.

**How to use it.** A `scalar` block names the tracers; the bound needs the EOS limiter
({{< code src/scalar/scalar_options.cpp ScalarOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}):

```yaml
dynamics:
  equation-of-state:
    limiter: true          # required by upper-bound > 0
scalar:
  names: [dye]             # sets nvar = 1
  upper-bound: 1.0         # default -1: no bound
  # reconstruct omitted: the hydro's horizontal reconstruction is used
  # riemann-solver omitted: upwind
```

Refused at setup ({{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::reset >}}):

1. A solver other than `upwind` ("[Scalar] Passive scalars currently require the upwind solver"), because the
   tracer flux is the dry-mass flux times the upwind ratio. A `scalar/riemann-solver` block without `type` takes the
   YAML fallback described in @sec-ch04-riemann and is refused too; omit the block to get `upwind`.
2. `upper-bound: 0` ("[Scalar] upper-bound = 0 pins the tracer to zero and freezes transport; use a negative value to
   disable the bound").
3. A positive bound without the limiter ("[Scalar] upper-bound needs the eos limiter"), because the bound from above
   is the positivity of the complement, and enforcing one side alone leaves the other unbounded.

The bound of @eq-ch10-tracer-bound is these lines ({{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::forward >}}):

```cpp
    auto theta = flux_positivity_theta(b * rho - u, g1, g2, g3, pcoord, dt);
    ...
    flux_positivity_scale_(sync_theta(theta), g1, g2, g3, pcoord);
    ...
    if (_flux1.defined()) _flux1.add_(h1 - g1);
```

with `b * rho - u` the complement of step 1, `g1` $=F^{\mathrm c}_n$ before scaling (kept as `h1`) and $\Theta F^{\mathrm c}_n$
after, so the last line adds $(1-\Theta)F^{\mathrm c}_n$ as in step 4.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_scalar.release` | bound holds on both sides | $10^{-12}$; $10^{-5}$ f32 | test thresholds |
| `test_tracer_dry_convention_python` | init, implicit and relax arms | $10^{-12}$ | 1000-fold non-vacuity |
| `test_forcing.release` | dry source keeps scalar bounds | $10^{-12}$ | test threshold |
| `test_dry_carry_zero_base_python` | the 0/0 guard of the carry | $10^{-12}$ abs. | test threshold |

: Tests of the dry-air tracers; all pass at the pin (@tbl-ch10-ctest-run). {#tbl-ch10-tracer-tests}

`scalar_upper_bound_holds_both_sides` advects 12 steps with the bound at 1 and requires
$r_n\le1+10^{-12}$ and $\rho_{\mathrm d}r_n\ge-10^{-12}$ in float64 ($10^{-5}$ in float32)
({{< code tests/test_scalar.cpp DeviceTest.scalar_upper_bound_holds_both_sides >}}).
`test_tracer_dry_convention` uses `TOL` $=10^{-12}$ and also requires each arm's signal to exceed 1000 times `TOL`, so
a pass is not vacuous ({{< code tests/test_tracer_dry_convention.py TOL >}}).
`test_scalar_flux_covariance_python` carries one tracer both as a scalar and as a hydro species and requires the
two to agree to `TOL` $=10^{-12}$ relative after 10 steps, with the covariance on and off
({{< code tests/test_scalar_flux_covariance.py >}}); `test_scalar_cov_x1_split_python` requires four in-process
$x_1$ blocks to match one block to $10^{-13}$ ({{< code tests/test_scalar_cov_x1_split.py >}}).
`test_stage_forcing_dry_tracer_python` and `test_flux_positivity_cubedsphere_python` (seams) are also registered.
Every ctest named here that the CPU build registers passed at the pin (@tbl-ch10-ctest-run); the CUDA and Gloo arms are not
registered in that build and were not run.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
When the card omits `scalar/reconstruct`, the scalars use the horizontal reconstruction of the hydro block; an
options object built in code without one has no such default. The upper bound holds only while the mass Courant number is
below one and the dry density moves by transport alone.
:::

- `ScalarOptions` has `thermo` and `kinetics` members that the YAML reader never fills. Set from code, they make
  `ScalarImpl::reset` build a `ThermoX` and a `Kinetics` module that nothing in `src/scalar` then calls
  (`pkinetics`, {{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::reset >}}).
- A uniform-tracer test cannot detect a wrong donor choice (docstring of `test_tracer_dry_convention.py`).
- Not in the switch coverage matrix (@sec-ch12-matrix).

Never written $r$ without its species subscript, because $r$ alone is the radius (§1)

[^rg-28a461114d30]: names — names of the passive scalars, one per scalar (in the `scalar` block)

[^rg-a7c011b0d04d]: upper-bound — upper bound for the scalar ratio; a negative value disables the bound
